text: Starting the test audit: reading every suite under tests/ to classify assertions as outcome, mechanism or fossil, ranked by risk.

Read 30 of ~46 tracked suites. Early shortlist: export-bundling-runtime and board-save-export-runtime are pure source-regex fossils (nothing anywhere actually exports a bundle in a browser); resize-handle-clipping is all computed style; vnc-node case G asserts window.__vncLeak which no code ever sets.

The audit found a live regression, not just a weak test. Ctrl+S never POSTs /api/save-board on the current runtime: in Chrome it opens a native Save-As dialog, in Firefox it downloads a .canvas. board-save-reload-e2e passes because a 19.4s autosave satisfies its waitForResponse, and board-save-export-runtime passes because its greedy regex finds saveBoard() 800 lines away. Proved with a timing probe.

Audit done. Four findings proved by breaking the feature in a mirrored tree and watching the suite stay green: bundle export (nothing anywhere clicks Export .zip), Ctrl+S, the recommendation .canvas.diff (filename checked, contents never opened), and the 'Older local draft was archived' data-loss guard (one regex on a toast string). Report at .agents/whiteboard/test_audit_2026-08-01.md, new suite tests/export/export-bundle-download-e2e.test.mjs, replacements in .tmp/scratch/opus5-25/proposed/, one runtime hunk needing the user in patch.json.
